subject: Discovery recap: Private/VPC requirements for Greenfield Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Rivera <alan.rivera@greenfieldhealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Private/VPC requirements for Greenfield Health

Hi Alan,

Thanks for taking time today. Quick recap from our discussion and next steps:

Pain points and goals:
- Need a private deployment option for PHI workloads subject to HIPAA and internal security controls.
- Minimize egress and ensure customer-managed keys for encryption at rest.
- Ability to run inference in a VPC with strict network controls and optional air-gapped on-prem for the highest-sensitivity projects.

Current stack:
- AWS (us-east-1) primary cloud account; some on-prem VMs in our data center.
- Using AWS KMS and an internal HSM for key management today.

Success criteria:
- VPC peering or private link to Redwood control plane; no public internet egress for inference data.
- Bring-Your-Own-Key support (KMS/HSM) with key rotation and audit logs.
- SOC 2 evidence and ability to run a short PoC in a non-prod VPC within 4 weeks.

Technical constraints discussed:
- Strict outbound rules; only specific endpoints allowed for telemetry.
- Potential air-gap requirement for one environment (no outbound connectivity).

Proposed next steps:
1) I will share a proposed architecture diagram and our private-deploy checklist (attached).
2) Dev Patel will scope a technical deep dive and confirm feasibility around the air-gap option.
3) Procurement: please share your standard security questionnaire and an AWS account ID for VPC peering testing.
4) We'll aim to schedule the deep dive next week; please let me know your availability.

Attachments:
- greenfield_network_diagram.png (stub)
- gf_privacy_questionnaire_sensitivity.docx (stub)

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

From: Alan Rivera <alan.rivera@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@greenfieldhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Private/VPC requirements for Greenfield Health

Hi Marissa,

Appreciate the clear summary that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:
- We can provide an AWS account ID for VPC peering in us-east-1 (123456789012).
- For key management we prefer BYOK via AWS KMS with key material wrapped by our HSM. We also need key rotation documentation and audit log access.
- The air-gap environment is required for one of our clinical analytics projects; here 'air-gap' means no egress to public internet and only manual syncs via approved media.
- Our security team will need SOC 2 and any relevant pen test reports.

Procurement will also want a rough pricing estimate and an NDA before we share more detailed diagrams. Please send an NDA template and any preliminary pricing bands for a PoC and annual dedicated/private deployment.

Thanks,
Alan Rivera
Director, Infrastructure Security | Greenfield Health
alan.rivera@greenfieldhealth.com

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Rivera <alan.rivera@greenfieldhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Private/VPC requirements for Greenfield Health

Alan / Marissa,

Thanks, a few technical questions to help scope the PoC and air-gap option:
1) Expected throughput for inference (tokens/sec or qps) and typical request size (avg prompt + response token count).
2) Which models are you planning to run? Any constraints on model size or quantization (we support quantized variants but need to validate quality).
3) For the air-gap environment: can you confirm how updates would be handled (e.g., periodic signed bundle imports, physical media transfer)?
4) Outbound egress: will you allow connections to our control plane for metrics/health or do you require fully offline operation?
5) Any strict IP allowlist we should be aware of for the peering test.

I'll attach our private deployment checklist and a short questionnaire to capture these details. If you can populate and return, it will speed the scoping.

Attachments:
- private_deploy_checklist.pdf (stub)

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai
